question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed opt-in canonical readiness contract, including required/advisory conditions and activation-scoped plugin providers, as public Gateway and plugin API surface?
rationale: This patch is a normative RFC for new configuration and extension contracts; Markdown review cannot determine whether these are the permanent supported product boundaries.

options.title: Accept readiness v1 direction
options.body: Approve the opt-in activation, required/advisory aggregation, and bounded provider model, then continue the linked implementation PR sequence.

options.title: Narrow to core conditions
options.body: Accept core readiness normalization first and defer public plugin-provider registration until its API has a separate decision.

options.title: Defer the RFC
options.body: Keep the legacy readiness model while maintainers define a different Gateway health and extension strategy.

recommendation.title: Accept readiness v1 direction
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in activation, required/advisory aggregation, and bounded provider model, then continue the linked implementation PR sequence.

likelyOwner.reason: A Gateway/plugin API owner must make this contract decision, but the available review evidence does not identify a concrete person with that remit.
